concerns.text: FR-001 requires downloading experimental $T_g$ data from the Polymer Genome Project and NIST WebBook. Task T005 instead downloads a SMILES parquet file from a HuggingFace URL, which does not provide $T_g$ values and is not a primary source, leaving FR-001 uncovered.
FR-001 also mandates acquisition of experimental $T_g$ data. Task T006 downloads Van Krevelen fragment contributions, unrelated to $T_g$, further failing to satisfy the functional requirement.
The spec requires filtering for amorphous homopolymers and binary blends (FR-001 scope). No task in the checklist performs this filtering, so the acceptance criterion is dropped.

Descriptor engineering (T008) creates a feature matrix without first ensuring that only the polymers meeting the FR-001 scope (amorphous homopolymers/binary blends) are present, potentially violating the scoped data requirement.
Physical‑property calculation (T010) applies Van Krevelen formulas to *all* polymers, ignoring the FR-001 scope filter, thereby extending the dataset beyond what the specification permits.

All $T_g$‑dependent tasks (T011–T018) are marked as conditional and are skipped when no $T_g$ file is found. Since FR-001 is a mandatory requirement, skipping these steps constitutes a weakening of the functional requirement rather than a staged implementation.

Principle I (Data Integrity) of the constitution demands raw data be fetched from primary sources (Polymer Genome Project, NIST). Task T005 sources data from a HuggingFace mirror, violating the constitutional principle.
Similarly, Task T006 obtains Van Krevelen fragments from a GitHub repository, not from a primary, vetted source, breaching Principle I.

Constitution Principle VI requires validation of EBM feature importance against WLF constants ($C_1$, $C_2$). The task list (T017, T018) validates against Fractional Free Volume and Chain Stiffness instead, constituting a direct drift from the constitution.
The same drift appears in T018, which performs sensitivity analysis based on FFV/Chain Stiffness rather than the mandated WLF constants, further violating Principle VI.

The plan and tasks defer the entire $T_g$ acquisition (FR-001) citing a “spec‑root kickback” without amending the specification to allow staging. This is a silent weakening of a non‑negotiable functional requirement.
